ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The image is a schematic diagram of an aquarium/nitrogen cycle. On the right side there is a fish, above the fish there is granular food and it is labeled A, and beside the fish there is B. Red arrows point from the fish and food area to a series of boxes at the bottom, such as G, D, J, etc., indicating waste or organic matter undergoing transformation. On the left side there is an aquatic plant, labeled H beside it. In the center there is a large box labeled F; a yellow arrow from F points left toward the aquatic plant, and another yellow arrow points upward toward C. Reasoning: In the aquarium nitrogen cycle, fish waste and leftover food are gradually transformed by bacteria, eventually forming a nitrogen nutrient form that plants can absorb and use. The final form mainly absorbed by aquatic plants is nitrate (硝酸盐). In the image, F is the nutrient label flowing toward the plant, therefore F is nitrate.
